notes.body: Would it make sense to to this in `extcap/CMakeLists.txt:set_extcap_executable_properties` instead?

I like the expressiveness and consistency and don't mind the repetition.

If it's OK with you I'd prefer to leave it as is.
It would make sense though, I'm OK with doing that.
`etwdump` is not building on MinGW but it would not be an issue, I think.
Same question as above, but for `set_extra_executable_properties`.
That would fail for dftest and probably others, I believe. I did not test it though, since a few months back.
I assumed we were using wmain everywhere on Windows. Given that and the comments above I'm OK with this as-is.

`target_link_options` was added in CMake 3.13. Unfortunately, the CentOS 8 builder is running 3.11: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/jobs/1609614539#L351

macOS x64 Buildbot is failing with:

```
CMake Error at extcap/CMakeLists.txt:122 (target_link_options):
  Unknown CMake command "target_link_options".
```

Buildbot needs updated CMake?
Thanks, I should have caught that. It only needs to run on Windows and our minimum version there is 3.13 so it's not a problem. I'll push something later to fix it.

commits_data.title: MinGW-w64: Need to link using -municode
commits_data.message:
MinGW-w64: Need to link using -municode

Some targets are not using unicode/WinMain (not sure why), so this
really needs to be a per target setting (better anyway).

commits_data.title: MinGW-w64: Use clock_gettime()
commits_data.message:
MinGW-w64: Use clock_gettime()

Mingw-w64 has this function. We may have to define some extra symbols
for API visibility but on my system the config check is working out
of the box.

POSIX systems come in many flavours, remove the "save time" if()
condition in this case.

Fix code to check if we have clock_gettime() on Windows as well.

commits_data.title: MinGW-w64: No need to define 'ssize_t'
commits_data.message:
MinGW-w64: No need to define 'ssize_t'

This will trigger a collision on MinGW-w64.

Define this instead for Microsoft's compiler.

We should probably have a compile time check instead.
